displayedInputs.question:
An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of \(40^\circ\). What is the measure of a base angle? (Unit: degrees; enter a number)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=AC\), \(\angle A=36^\circ\), and \(BD\) bisects \(\angle ABC\), intersecting \(AC\) at \(D\). Among \(\triangle ABC\), \(\triangle ABD\), and \(\triangle BCD\), how many are isosceles triangles? (Enter a number.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(\angle A=30^\circ\), and \(AB=10\). What is \(BC\)? (Enter a numerical value.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

\(A\) and \(B\) lie on the same side of line \(l\). The distance from \(A\) to \(l\) is \(3\), the distance from \(B\) to \(l\) is \(6\), and the distance between the feet of the perpendiculars from \(A\) and \(B\) to \(l\) is \(12\). Point \(P\) moves along \(l\). Find the minimum value of \(PA+PB\).

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

The legs have lengths 6 and 8. How long is the hypotenuse? (Right triangle; the result is an integer.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 13 and a leg of length 5. Find the length of the other leg.

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

In the hypotenuse diagram, the large square has side length \(c\), and four right triangles with legs \(a\) and \(b\) enclose a small square. How can \(a^2+b^2=c^2\) be obtained? (Assume \(b>a\) and select the correct derivation.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

In the hypotenuse diagram, each of the four right triangles has legs of lengths 3 and 4. Find the area of the large square (whose side length is the hypotenuse \(c\)). (Calculate by adding the areas of the 4 triangles and the central small square.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)
